data.result:
I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's a comprehensive setup guide:

## Server-Side Setup

Run these commands on your server:

```bash
# 1. Create git repository directory
sudo mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
sudo git init --bare
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /git  # or appropriate user

# 2. Create web directory
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/server
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /var/www/server

# 3. Set up git hook for auto-deployment
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/server git checkout -f
EOF

chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive

# 4. Initialize the web directory with the repo content
git clone /git/server /tmp/server-deploy
cd /tmp/server-deploy
git config user.email "deploy@server"
git config user.name "Deploy"
cd /var/www/server
git init
git remote add origin /git/server
git fetch origin
git checkout -t origin/master

# 5. Set up web server (nginx)
sudo apt-get install -y nginx

# Create nginx config
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/server > /dev/null << 'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/server;
    index index.html;
    
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
EOF

# Enable the site
sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/server /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/server
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default  # Remove default if it exists

# Test and restart nginx
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

## Local Client Setup

On your local computer:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server
cd server
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master

# Test it works
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

## How It Works

1. **Bare Repository**: `/git/server` is a bare repository (no working directory) that acts as the central hub
2. **Post-receive Hook**: When you push, the hook automatically checks out the latest code to `/var/www/server`
3. **Web Server**: Nginx serves files from `/var/www/server` on port 8080

Any push to `master` will automatically update the deployed files. You can add more sophisticated hooks later (CI/CD, build steps, etc.) by modifying the `post-receive` script.

Let me know if you hit any issues with permissions or want to customize the setup further!

I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. Here's a comprehensive setup guide:

## Server-Side Setup

Run these commands on your server:

```bash
# 1. Create git repository directory
sudo mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
sudo git init --bare
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /git  # or appropriate user

# 2. Create web directory
sudo mkdir -p /var/www/server
sudo chown -R $(whoami) /var/www/server

# 3. Set up git hook for auto-deployment
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
GIT_WORK_TREE=/var/www/server git checkout -f
EOF

chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive

# 4. Initialize the web directory with the repo content
git clone /git/server /tmp/server-deploy
cd /tmp/server-deploy
git config user.email "deploy@server"
git config user.name "Deploy"
cd /var/www/server
git init
git remote add origin /git/server
git fetch origin
git checkout -t origin/master

# 5. Set up web server (nginx)
sudo apt-get install -y nginx

# Create nginx config
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/server > /dev/null << 'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/server;
    index index.html;
    
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
EOF

# Enable the site
sudo ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/server /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/server
sudo rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default  # Remove default if it exists

# Test and restart nginx
sudo nginx -t
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

## Local Client Setup

On your local computer:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server
cd server
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master

# Test it works
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
```

## How It Works

1. **Bare Repository**: `/git/server` is a bare repository (no working directory) that acts as the central hub
2. **Post-receive Hook**: When you push, the hook automatically checks out the latest code to `/var/www/server`
3. **Web Server**: Nginx serves files from `/var/www/server` on port 8080

Any push to `master` will automatically update the deployed files. You can add more sophisticated hooks later (CI/CD, build steps, etc.) by modifying the `post-receive` script.

Let me know if you hit any issues with permissions or want to customize the setup further!
